faqs.a: The award sets minimum rates for electrical workers. For a grade 5 employee with all applicable allowances (industry, tool and electrician's licence), the hourly rate is $32.19, weekly $1,223.11. That works out to roughly $63,601 a year for a 38-hour week. Many electricians earn above the award, but this is the legal minimum.

faqs.q: How is tax calculated on an electrician's annual salary?

For a $63,601 salary, tax would be roughly $9,267 plus Medicare $1,272, leaving about $53,062 after tax.

faqs.q: What is the casual rate for an electrician under the award?

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Average Electrician Salary Australia

When searching for the **average electrician salary Australia**, it helps to start with the minimum rates set by the Fair Work Commission. The Electrical, Electronic and Communications Contracting Award 2020 (MA000025) covers most electricians and electrical workers. The award includes several classification levels (grades 1 to 10) and various allowances that add to the base rate.

For a qualified electrician, a common classification is Electrical worker grade 5. Under the award, the minimum weekly rate for a full-time grade 5 employee is $1,119.10, or $29.45 per hour. But most electricians also receive an industry allowance, a tool allowance, and if they hold an electrician’s licence, a licence allowance. When all three are included, the grade 5 rate becomes $1,223.11 per week, or $32.19 per hour. That is the all-purpose rate used for calculating overtime, leave, and public holidays.

### From Hourly to Annual: The Calculation

To convert an hourly rate to an annual salary, use the formula:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

We assume a standard 38-hour week, as set out in the award. For the grade 5 electrician with allowances:

- Hourly: $32.19
- Weekly: $32.19 × 38 = $1,223.11 (matches the award)
- Fortnightly: $1,223.11 × 2 = $2,446.22
- Annual: $1,223.11 × 52 = $63,601.72 (or $32.19 × 38 × 52)

This is the minimum annual salary for that classification. Many electricians earn more through over-award payments, overtime, or higher grades. The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports average weekly earnings for full-time adult employees at $2,083.70 (May 2026), which would be about $108,352 per year. That figure includes all occupations, not just electricians.

### Tax and Medicare on Your Electrician Salary

Once you have your annual gross figure, you can estimate your take-home pay using the 2026-27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% of excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 + 30% of excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 + 37% of excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: $51,370 + 45% of excess over $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% of taxable income (with possible reductions for low-income earners).

For a $63,601 salary:
- Tax: $4,020 + 30% × ($63,601 – $45,000) = $4,020 + $5,580.30 = $9,600.30
- Medicare: $63,601 × 2% = $1,272.02
- After-tax: $63,601 – $9,600 – $1,272 = $52,729 (rounded)

Note: This does not include the Medicare levy surcharge or HELP repayments. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a more detailed estimate.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Employers must pay superannuation guarantee contributions of 12% of ordinary earnings (for 2026-27) on top of your salary. The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per quarter. For a $63,601 salary, super is $63,601 × 12% = $7,632.12 per year, added to your super fund, not to your take-home pay.

### Casual Loading for Electricians

If you work as a casual electrician, you receive a 25% loading instead of paid leave and other entitlements. The casual hourly rate is the ordinary rate plus 25%. For grade 5 with allowances: $32.19 × 1.25 = $40.24 per hour. Overtime and penalty rates are then calculated from this loaded rate. See our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page for more.

### Award vs. Market Rates

The award rates are the legal minimum. The actual **average electrician salary Australia** may be higher. Recruiter surveys often quote figures around $90,000 to $110,000 for experienced electricians, but these are not official. For reliable minimums, always refer to the Fair Work Ombudsman’s [pay guides](/blog) and the Fair Work Commission’s award. The ABS provides broader earnings data, but not specific to electricians.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. It then shows your weekly, fortnightly, monthly, and annual pay, plus estimated tax and super. Remember: enter your base rate *before* casual loading – the calculator adds the 25% if you check the box.

### Summary

For a grade 5 electrician under the Electrical Award, the minimum hourly rate including key allowances is $32.19, giving an annual salary of about $63,600. After tax and Medicare, take-home pay is roughly $52,700, with super of $7,600 paid on top. Use our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page to compare with other occupations, and always check the latest award for your specific classification.
